note: Frontier Moto does not sell equipment and takes no commission. Items appear here because they were used on a route or inspected in person. Where we have not tested something, it is marked untested.

gear.name: Full face helmet, vented
gear.summary: Ventilation matters more than weight at equatorial midday. A quiet helmet that cooks you is the wrong helmet.

gear.name: Two piece rain suit over armour
gear.summary: Survives a full season if the seams are taped and it goes over armour rather than under it. Packs smaller than a one piece.

gear.name: Dry bag with compression straps
gear.summary: Cheaper, lighter and more waterproof than hard cases, and it does not change the width of the bike in traffic.

gear.name: Dual purpose, road biased
gear.summary: For riders who meet murram occasionally rather than daily. A knobbly tyre used mostly on tarmac is a braking problem.

gear.name: Tyre plug kit and compact inflator
gear.summary: The single highest value item per gram carried. Practise on a dead tyre at home before you need it on a shoulder.

spec.v: A plug is a repair to get you home

gear.name: Reflective vest, class rated
gear.summary: We have not run a controlled comparison. Any rated vest beats none, and the one you actually wear beats the better one you leave at home.

listings.title: 150 cc commuter, single owner
listings.detail: Service history present, chain set recent, tyres at half.
listings.description: One owner commuter kept on a written service routine. Starts clean, idles steady, chain and sprockets recent. Tyres at roughly half, priced to allow a fresh rear within the season.

specs.v: Chain set recent, tyres at half

listings.faults: Honest wear on paint and seat cover. Nothing structural found at inspection.

listings.title: 250 cc dual sport
listings.detail: Higher mileage, fork seals weeping, otherwise sound.
listings.description: Leggy but honest dual sport that has done real distance. Engine pulls clean through the range and the chassis tracks straight. Fork seals are weeping and priced into the number.
listings.faults: Fork seals weeping. Budget for seals and fork oil before a long route.

listings.title: 125 cc, stage retired
listings.detail: Working machine, honest wear, priced accordingly.
listings.description: Retired working bike with honest wear and no surprises at inspection. A practical first machine or a spare for the shamba run, priced for its condition rather than its story.
listings.faults: Cosmetic wear on plastics and rack. Consumables due on normal schedule.

listings.title: 400 cc adventure, imported
listings.detail: Low mileage, no local service history, parts lead time is the risk.
listings.description: Low mileage import with no local service history on file. Clean presentation and tidy running gear. The risk is parts lead time rather than condition, so check shelf availability before committing.
listings.faults: No faults found on a visual check. Full inspection recommended before purchase.

listings.title: Aluminium pannier set with mounts
listings.detail: Scuffed cases, straight mounts, seals intact and dry inside.
listings.description: Second hand pannier set removed after a bike change. Cases are scuffed from use but mounts are straight, latches close properly and seals kept dust out on a dry run.
listings.faults: Scuffs and one shallow dent on the left case. No cracks or leaks.

listings.title: Field tool roll with plug kit
listings.detail: Complete roadside roll, used but complete, inflator tested working.
listings.description: Pre owned roadside roll covering punctures, fasteners and chain adjustment. Plug kit unused, inflator tested working, spanners with normal workshop marks.
listings.faults: Normal tool marks. One tyre lever shows grinding from a previous repair.

supply.status: No checkout here. Every listing below is second hand and sold by its owner, not by Frontier Moto. Prices are set by sellers. Frontier notes condition and inspection honestly and takes no commission.
standards: Used on a route or inspected in person before it is listed
Suited to heat, dust, load and poor fuel before it is suited to a catalogue
Repairable where possible, and marked honestly where it is not
Priced against what it replaces, not what it promises
supply.price_note: A fair price follows condition, history and parts availability, in that order. Condition is what the machine is today. History is what was done, by whom, and how long ago in kilometres. Parts availability is the risk most buyers underweight: a sound machine with a six week parts lead time is a different purchase from the same machine with parts on the shelf.
